applies_why: Yes: it grounds UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse's admission of two readings.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. — I weighed whether admitted two readings make the verse not open, so UNDERDETERMINED is barred, versus K-S2 only barring a no-statement ground, so ambiguity could still be UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The judge text treats Matthew 1:16's two admitted readings as an open UNDERDETERMINED result, but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.
